ai.description: *Raorchestes uthamani* is a small frog (22–25 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and distinct reddish-brown blotches. It features a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin on the belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes uthamani* is best distinguished by the unique, bright yellow or golden-yellow coloration on its hidden surfaces, specifically the groin and inner thighs.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes uthamani inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes uthamani is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects among the forest foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes uthamani* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It lays small clutches of eggs in leaf axils during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes uthamani* is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests and grasslands of the Anamalai Hills in the Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes uthamani* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from the canopy of evergreen forests.
